upstream.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.

classification.analysis: Matt Pocock's personal, heavily-starred collection of AI-agent engineering skills ('Skills for Real Engineers') covering requirement-gathering interviews (grill-me), domain-modeling/shared-language docs, spec-to-tickets breakdown, TDD, debugging, and codebase-architecture review, designed to be small, composable, and model-agnostic rather than owning the whole dev process like GSD, BMAD, or Spec-Kit. Distributed as a Claude Code plugin (managed, read-only) or via the skills.sh installer (editable copies) for Codex and other agents; splits skills into user-invoked (slash commands) versus model-invoked (auto-triggered) categories.

use_cases.title: Run a grilling interview to align an agent on unclear requirements
Break a plan or spec into dependency-ordered tracer-bullet tickets
Drive red-green-refactor TDD from an agent skill
Survey a codebase for architecture-deepening opportunities
